transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Kaur (Redwood Security), Priya Raman (CISO, Veridian), Tom Alvarez (Director of IT), Sara Li (Procurement), Ben Torres (Cloud Architect)

Summary (auto): Walkthrough of SIG questionnaire and evidence requirements. Discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO options, audit log retention, data residency, encryption/KMS and next steps for evidence handoff.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna run through the SIG today, uh quick intro, i'm lena with redwood inference, marcus is our solutions eng, aisha is on security.
[00:12] Priya Raman: Hi, thanks. i'm priya, ciso at veridian. we'll mainly be focusing on data residency and KMS integration.
[00:20] Marcus Chen: great. quick agenda, SOC 2 / ISO statements, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, encryption and then the SIG answers plus evidence links.
[00:32] Tom Alvarez: Sounds good. our procurement timeline is end of may, so need to know what evidence we can see asap.
[00:39] Aisha Kaur: to set expectations, our SOC 2 Type II report is current through 2026-03, we also have ISO 27001 certification in our roadmap but not yet certified, we can share current controls mapping.
[00:52] Sara Li: when you say "share SOC 2", is that the full report or redacted? procurement prefers redacted but security team wants full if possible under NDA.
[01:03] Lena Ortiz: we typically provide the full SOC 2 under NDA; we can also provide a redacted executive summary in parallel.
[01:11] Ben Torres: for private deployments, we need to confirm VPC and KMS support — specifically customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or HSM.
[01:20] Marcus Chen: yes, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for Redwood Private, and we integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. for hosted api we use our managed KMS but we offer encryption at rest and in transit; we can document the KMS key lifecycle and rotations.
[01:37] Priya Raman: and for hosted — does data ever leave region? our requirement is EU data residency for EU customers.
[01:44] Aisha Kaur: for hosted we support regional tenancy; data for EU pinned customers stays in the eu-west region. we'll include the network flow diagram.
[01:52] Tom Alvarez: audit logs — retention? we need 12 months of immutable logs, search/exports, and access to tamper-evident trails.
[02:03] Marcus Chen: audit logs are stored centrally, default retention 90 days, but for enterprise we can extend to 13 months with the compliance add-on. logs are stored with integrity checks and we provide syslog/S3 export for archival.
[02:16] Priya Raman: can we integrate with our SIEM? Splunk is what we use.
[02:19] Marcus Chen: yes, we have connector options — push and pull. we'll share details and runbook.
[02:25] [00:02:30] Marcus Chen: switching to RBAC and SSO — single sign on via SAML/Okta is supported, SCIM for user provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC for roles and route-level permissions.
[02:43] Priya Raman: do you have separation of duties for service accounts vs human users?
[02:48] Aisha Kaur: yes we recommend using managed service principals; service keys are scoped and auditable. we rotate keys automatically on private deployments and advise time-limited tokens for hosted.
[02:59] Sara Li: procurement question — subprocessors list? we need to know third parties and data handling agreements.
[03:08] Lena Ortiz: we'll attach our current subprocessors list; top ones are AWS, GCP for region-specific infra, and certain CDN partners. we have executed DPA and can share the template.
[03:18] Ben Torres: on the SIG spreadsheet specifically, are there prefilled answers or do you want us to complete?
[03:24] Marcus Chen: we prefill a baseline of answers and mark where we need evidence. then we add links to artifacts in a secure S3 bucket or customer-facing portal.
[03:33] Priya Raman: evidence examples — do you have pen test reports? vulnerability scanning cadence?
[03:38] Aisha Kaur: yes, annual third-party penetration tests with executive summary available; full reports are shared under NDA. internal vuln scanning is weekly for infra, daily for container images, and we have CVE triage process.
[03:51] Tom Alvarez: regarding data deletion, if a tenant requests deletion, how do you ensure all backups and caches are purged?
[04:00] Marcus Chen: we have documented deletion workflows: soft-delete triggers cascade and backup retention policies are aligned; for private deployments we can run a verification job and provide attestation. for hosted customers we provide SLA'd deletion windows — we'll include the flow.
[04:15] [00:04:30] Priya Raman: on encryption in transit — TLS versions and cert management?
[04:20] Aisha Kaur: TLS 1.2 minimum, 1.3 preferred; certs managed by our platform with rotation and support for customer-managed certs for custom domains.
[04:31] Sara Li: tokenization of PII — do you provide any PII redaction or masking features?
[04:36] Marcus Chen: we have optional pre-processing hooks for redaction and a configurable pipeline; commonly customers use that together with selective logging to reduce exposure.
[04:45] Ben Torres: latency/cost tradeoffs aside, for dedicated capacity can we ensure private subnets for model serving nodes?
[04:52] Marcus Chen: yes dedicated capacity runs in customer VPC for Private deployments and we support private subnets, no public IPs on serving nodes.
[05:00] [00:05:30] Priya Raman: can you map specific SIG questions to SOC controls? we'd like to see direct traceability.
[05:07] Aisha Kaur: we already maintain a mapping doc (SOC control -> SIG/CAIQ question) and we'll attach it; that helps audit teams cross-walk quickly.
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: any known gaps or compensating controls we should be aware of?
[05:22] Marcus Chen: the main gap is ISO 27001 — we have policy and controls in place but certification is in process; compensating controls include stricter internal audits and additional logging for the affected domains.
[05:33] Priya Raman: legal will look at data processing addendum and subprocessor clause, procurement needs the DPA and standard terms.
[05:40] Lena Ortiz: we can send the DPA template and a redlined sample for enterprise customers.
[05:46] [00:06:30] Sara Li: timeline — if we sign off end of may, when can we onboard into dedicated capacity?
[05:54] Marcus Chen: for dedicated capacity typical lead time is 4-6 weeks after contract signature for standard configurations; expedited options exist with additional fees.
[06:03] Ben Torres: small nit — do you rotate KMS keys automatically or do we manage rotations?
[06:07] Aisha Kaur: for customer-managed KMS customers manage rotation policy; for our managed keys we rotate and can provide rotation logs.
[06:15] [00:07:00] Priya Raman: any SOC exceptions or open findings in last report?
[06:20] Lena Ortiz: there were a couple of low-severity findings around access reviews; we've closed one and have remediation timeline for the other, which we'll include in the SOC report notes.
[06:31] Marcus Chen: moving to evidence handoff — we'll share a secure link to an S3 bucket with pre-signed links for documents; docs include SOC 2 report, pen test exec summaries, subprocessors, architecture diagrams, and the filled SIG spreadsheet.
[06:48] Sara Li: prefer a link to a secure portal rather than raw S3 links.
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: noted, we'll enable a portal view for Veridian and send an NDA before full reports.
[06:59] [00:07:30] Priya Raman: for audit logs being tamper-evident, can you provide certificates or attestations?
[07:05] Aisha Kaur: we can provide hash chains and integrity proofs and export formats for ingestion into your archive. we'll attach sample exports.
[07:16] Tom Alvarez: one more — do you allow periodic audit support, like access for our auditors?
[07:20] Marcus Chen: yes we offer auditor access models: in-person review, remote access under NDA, or receiving exported artifacts. details depend on contract.
[07:30] [00:08:00] Priya Raman: ok that's helpful. next steps?
[07:34] Lena Ortiz: recap — we'll send SOC 2 Type II under NDA, the prefilled SIG with evidence links, subprocessors list, architecture diagram, and a runbook for SIEM integration. we'll also schedule a follow-up to review the evidence.
[07:48] Sara Li: procurement wants pricing and SLA add-on notes as well.
[07:52] Lena Ortiz: yes we'll include pricing options for Dedicated/Private and the compliance add-on pricing for extended log retention.
[07:59] [00:08:30] Priya Raman: we'll confirm our exact data residency requirement and follow up with any extra evidence requests.
[08:06] Ben Torres: thanks everyone.
[08:09] Lena Ortiz: thanks all. we'll get the items over by friday.

End of transcript.

Notes: occasional transcription glitches on product names (redwood/private vs redwood dedicated) and acronyms; speaker labels are accurate to attendee list but Fireflies auto-labeling may have minor mismatches.
